what: Second audit corpus: harnesses harvested from the PROJECTS OWN REPOSITORIES, not just the OSS-Fuzz tree.
method: For each OSS-Fuzz C/C++ project with a github main_repo (478 of them), shallow-clone, copy out *fuzz*.{c,cc,cpp}, delete the clone. Disk stays flat.
scale_note: QuartetFuzz audited 586 harnesses across 70 projects. This is 1401 across both corpora, 278 of them at high fidelity.
oss_fuzz_tree_grew: 372 -> 420 purely from globbing .cpp, which the audit tool had never matched. 54 of the first 122 upstream harnesses were .cpp, so the omission was dropping nearly half a corpus without reporting it.

defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.free_verb_was_a_substring: "send" contains "end", so nghttp2_session_mem_send2 read as a DESTROY of the session. Now matched on underscore/camel segments, with strong verbs allowed as a prefix (freeaddrinfo) and short ones required to be the whole segment (endian, delimiter).
defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.member_free_attributed_to_the_struct: free(ctx.certificates.list[i].base) and free(ctx.certificates.list) both fell back to , so two member frees read as a double free of the struct (h2o/picotls).
defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.two_phase_teardown: lldpd_port_cleanup(port,1) then free(port) is correct -- cleanup releases members, the caller releases the object. Verified in lldpd src/lldpd-structs.c: port_cleanup does NOT free the port, chassis_cleanup DOES, which is why the same harness frees one and not the other. Reported at INFO.
defects_found_in_the_ENGINE_by_this_corp.double_create_ignored_ownership: pjsip parses twice into the same slot, both from a pool released at the end. Ownership knew; only the end-of-harness leak check was asking.

findings: 0 new upstream-reportable defects from this corpus so far. All 8 candidates triaged by reading; all 8 were defects in this engine.
standing_total: 1 confirmed finding (bluez fuzz_gobex GError leak, google/oss-fuzz#16081) from 26+8 = 34 candidates triaged.

SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.defect: pixAverageByRow is called with pix_pointer_payload after pixDestroy nulled it, and the block is missing the pixCopy every other block performs
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.verified: pixDestroy sets *ppix = NULL (src/pix1.c); pixAverageByRow returns immediately on !pix (src/pix3.c:2447)
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.class: dead coverage -- the function is never executed on any input, silently
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.note_on_the_label: The gate called it a use-after-free and a double free. Both are literally wrong, because the pointer is nulled rather than dangling. The SEQUENCE was real and reading it found a genuine defect of another kind.
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.status: NOT YET REPORTED -- needs the operator's go-ahead
SECOND_CONFIRMED_FINDING.scope_correction: The first patch fixed ONE of three instances and the gate still flagged two more. Filing it would have been a partial fix presented as complete. The file has three: a missing pixCopy before pixAverageByRow, a missing pixCopy before pixVarianceInRect, and pixVarianceByColumn passed `pix2` -- destroyed ten lines earlier -- while the pix_pointer_payload created directly above it goes unused.
